description: Adversaries may abuse the cron utility to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code. The cron utility is a time-based job scheduler for Unix-like operating systems. A crontab file contains the schedule of cron entries to be run and the specified times for execution. Cron may also be run interactively with variable and pathnames declared in a temporary file. Adversaries may use cron in Linux or Unix environments to execute programs at system startup or on a scheduled basis for persistence.

falco.trigger_condition: Write to /etc/cron.d/, /etc/cron.daily/, /etc/crontab, or /var/spool/cron/crontabs/ inside a container. Falco file write monitoring on cron directories provides persistence detection.

mitigation: Audit cron jobs regularly and alert on unexpected additions. Restrict crontab write access to authorized administrative accounts only. Use read-only root filesystems in containers to prevent cron directory modifications. Monitor for cron daemon execution of unexpected binaries.
